name: a_geopolitics_trade
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Geopolitics & trade.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
US-China relations (summits, trade truce, tariffs, export controls, chip rules, restrictions on foreign-made products or components — with the US stocks that benefit or lose), Iran / Middle East / Strait of Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine, sanctions — named officials, dates, terms, deadlines; latest status as of the cutoff.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **BA** / **GE** / **HON** — US–China aerospace trade [Macro / Geopolitics]

- The US Commerce Department slowed approvals for aircraft-part exports to China in recent weeks, limited approvals mainly to state-owned COMAC, and considered restricting aviation hydraulic-fluid shipments; China requested several years of spare parts for 200 Boeing jets purchased in spring 2026. The reported negotiations on rare earths and other economic disputes are scheduled to run through **January 10, 2027**. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, 04:56 ET)

- The reported export-licensing slowdown affects US aerospace suppliers including **Boeing (BA)**, **GE Aerospace (GE)** and **Honeywell (HON)**; the report identified the restrictions as leverage in US–China trade negotiations. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, 04:56 ET)

## US–China tariff truce [Macro / Geopolitics]

- The US and China extended their trade truce for **two months through January 10, 2027**, according to China’s Commerce Ministry. (Reuters, Sep. 28, 2026; republished Oct. 5, 2026, 02:03 ET)

- The countries agreed to reduce tariffs on approximately **€53 billion of goods imported from each other**; the US list included Chinese small appliances, tableware, linens, toys and holiday decorations, while China’s list included US agricultural products, seafood, wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. (Reuters, Sep. 27, 2026; republished Oct. 5, 2026, 02:03 ET)

## Iran / Strait of Hormuz [Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics]

- The Strait of Hormuz was reported as effectively closed amid the Iran conflict and attacks on shipping; the waterway had carried approximately **18 million barrels per day** before the conflict, while the seven-day moving average was reported at **18.5 million barrels per day on October 1**. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, publication time not stated)

- Middle East crude exports exceeded pre-war levels on **September 24 and September 27–29**, reaching **19.5 million to 22.5 million barrels per day**, according to provisional Kpler shipping data; LNG shipments through Hormuz reached their highest monthly level since February in September. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, publication time not stated)

- Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** said on Sunday, October 4, that Tehran’s proposal could restore security in the Strait of Hormuz within **seven days** if accepted; Iran also demanded sanctions relief, release of frozen funds, an end to hostilities and an end to the US naval blockade. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, publication time not stated)

- Iran’s oil minister **Mohsen Paknejad** resigned on Sunday, October 4, and acting minister **Hamid Bovard** took over as Iranian crude exports were reported to be constrained by the US blockade and sanctions scrutiny. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, publication time not stated)

- Iran’s crude production was reported at approximately **1.8 million barrels per day**, about half its pre-war output, while Iranian crude cargoes had not crossed the US blockade line toward China since mid-July and no new crude had been loaded at Iranian terminals since mid-August. [report] (Iran International, Oct. 5, 2026, 05:12 ET)

- The US Treasury’s sanctions announced on **October 1** targeted Iran’s largest automakers, including **Iran Khodro Company** and **SAIPA**, as well as the Islamic Republic of Iran Railway Company, Raja Passenger Trains Company and Railway Transportation Company. (Arab News, Oct. 5, 2026, 02:50 ET)

- The October 1 sanctions also covered foreign suppliers to Iran’s automotive and rail sectors under the Treasury’s **“Operation Economic Outcast,”** announced August 24. (Arab News, Oct. 5, 2026, 02:50 ET)

## **XOM** / **CVX** — Middle East oil-supply risk [Energy]

- Iranian oil exports were reported as “virtually zero” because of the US naval blockade, while Middle East crude volumes through the Strait of Hormuz were reported at approximately **14.19 million barrels per day** over the latest seven-day period, compared with a pre-war level of approximately **17.13 million barrels per day**. (Chosun, Oct. 5, 2026, 03:17 ET)

- Iran-backed Houthi militants were reported to have attacked shipping in the Red Sea, while Eritrea’s approximately **1,000-kilometer coastline** was described as an alternative shipping corridor to Hormuz. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, 02:20 ET)

## Russia sanctions [Macro / Geopolitics]

- US Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** said on October 4 that President **Donald Trump** had until **October 18** to decide whether to impose tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy, specifically identifying **China and India**. [report] (CBS News interview cited by NV, Oct. 5, 2026, 06:20 ET)

- The reported proposed tariffs would be authorized under the **Lindsey Graham Act**, signed by President Trump on **September 18, 2026**, which permits tariffs of up to **100%** on countries continuing to buy Russian energy and expands restrictions on Russia’s military, financial and energy sectors, foreign suppliers and “shadow fleet” vessels. [report] (NV, Oct. 5, 2026, 06:20 ET)

- Ukraine was reported to be preparing a list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals for potential sanctions under the Graham Act for presentation to the Trump administration and Congress during the week of October 5. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 5, 2026, 07:09 ET)
